decisions.reason: As a newly launched line with its own page and a close fit to the firm's engineered drainage system portfolio, it is likely to be retained unless early results clearly fall below aspiration levels.

This floor-level shower drainage system sits directly in the firm's strategic direction toward integrated low-profile bathroom solutions, so management would usually keep it while performance is still being learned.
Because it is presented as a flagship product and strongly matches the firm's design-led positioning, management is very unlikely to withdraw it after only a short market test absent obvious failure.
The integrated-slope shower element complements the firm's installation-ease value proposition, making continued support more likely than reallocation of resources at this early stage.

Its dedicated presentation and explicit problem-solving launch framing suggest management sees it as a meaningful niche addition, so it would likely remain unless sales quickly disappointed relative to expectations.

Although adjacent to the drainage business, the air-admittance valve appears more peripheral to the firm's main strategic thrust and only lightly featured, so it has the highest withdrawal risk but would still more likely be kept for now.
